insights.claim: The operator forces a pod restart when the OpenShift APIServer TLS security profile changes, ensuring runtime TLS configuration never drifts from the cluster-mandated profile.
insights.reasoning: The Bootstrap function reads the OpenShift TLS profile at startup and a SecurityProfileWatcher cancels the manager context on changes, causing a pod restart. This is a stricter enforcement pattern than runtime reconfiguration and ensures no window of TLS profile drift.

insights.claim: Both admission webhooks use failurePolicy: Fail, making workbenches-operator a blocking dependency for all Notebook CR create/update operations across the cluster.
insights.reasoning: With failurePolicy: Fail on both webhooks, any operator unavailability (crash, certificate expiry, network partition) blocks all notebook lifecycle operations. This is a deliberate security choice (connection secrets and hardware profiles must be validated) but creates an availability coupling.

insights.claim: The operator supports two TLS certificate providers (OpenShift service-ca and cert-manager) with runtime detection, enabling deployment on both OpenShift and non-OpenShift Kubernetes clusters.
insights.reasoning: The configureWebhookServingCerts function probes for service-ca availability and falls back to cert-manager, with the ability to disable webhooks entirely if neither provider is available. This dual-provider pattern enables the same operator binary to run across cluster topologies.
